title: Authorization Evidence Synthesis Guideline
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

This guideline defines a repeatable, automated approach for synthesizing compliance evidence that spans authorization (RBAC/ABAC), audit logging, data residency / retention, secure SDLC milestones, incident response artifacts, and the lifecycle of risk exceptions. It is intended for security engineers, SREs, platform owners, and compliance reviewers responsible for packaging evidence for audits and regulatory requests.

Key goals:
- Provide a single, auditable evidence package for a customer tenancy or internal system that maps controls to artifacts.
- Minimize manual steps by prescribing telemetry mappings, metadata standards, and extraction commands.
- Preserve data residency and retention constraints while meeting auditor needs.
- Formalize an exceptions lifecycle that surfaces residual risks with compensating controls.

Scope

Applies to: Redwood-hosted control plane and customer-facing inference endpoints; Dedicated and Private deployment documentation requirements remain consistent though data extraction methods differ (see "Extractors and Packaging" below). Does NOT replace product-level security attestations (SOC/ISO) but feeds evidence into those processes.

Principles

1) Evidence-first design: Logs and telemetry must be produced with a downstream export in mind (structured JSON, stable field names, consistent timestamps via UTC).
2) Least-privilege disclosure: When building evidence packages, redact or exclude unrelated PII or tenant data beyond auditor scope; include a redaction manifest.
3) Traceable lineage: Every artifact must include provenance headers (collector, commit/tag, extractor-run-id, timestamp).
4) Residency-aware exports: Evidence collectors must honor region-specific retention and export rules and produce a residency assertion file.

Authorization model and RBAC evidence

- Required artifacts:
  - Role catalog snapshot (CSV/JSON): role_id, role_name, permissions_list, owner_team, last_modified_commit
  - Role assignment export: subject_id (principal), role_id, assignment_granted_at, delegated_by, source (SCIM/CLI/API)
  - Privileged session logs: session_id, actor, start_ts, end_ts, actions_summary, justification_id (if requested)

- Evidence checks (automated):
  1. Verify no role in the catalog has wildcard resource: true unless approved exception exists.
  2. Confirm every privileged role has an owner_team and quarterly certification flag.
  3. Cross-verify role assignments against HR/IDP snapshots for termination events in the last 90 days.

Audit logging and telemetry mapping

Audit log schema (recommended stable fields):
- timestamp: ISO8601 UTC
- tenant_id: stable tenant identifier (if applicable)
- principal_id: user/service id
- principal_type: user|service|role
- action: canonical action string (e.g., model.generate, key.rotate, role.assign)
- resource_type: e.g., key, model, route, cluster
- resource_id: opaque id
- outcome: success|failure|denied
- request_id: correlation id
- latency_ms: integer
- details: free-form object (redact PII)

Sample audit entry (JSON):
{
  "timestamp": "2027-02-01T14:23:11Z",
  "tenant_id": "tenant-789",
  "principal_id": "svc-inference-23",
  "principal_type": "service",
  "action": "model.infer.call",
  "resource_type": "model",
  "resource_id": "gptx-1.2",
  "outcome": "success",
  "request_id": "req-1234abcd",
  "latency_ms": 132,
  "details": {"prompt_tokens": 78, "response_tokens": 54}
}

Data residency and retention mapping

Provide a residency assertion file alongside evidence: residency-assertion.txt containing region, export-method, retention-policy-reference, and hash of package. Example table for retention windows:

| Artifact | Minimum retention | Residency constraint | Redaction required? | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| Audit logs (structured) | 2 years | Same region as tenant | redact PII | eng-sre |
| Role assignments export | 3 years | Control-plane region | redact non-essential attributes | security |
| Privileged session recordings | 1 year | Control-plane region | exclude session payloads | eng-sre |
| Secure SDLC evidence (build logs, signed artifacts) | 5 years | US/EU (per contract) | include hashes only | platform-eng |

Secure SDLC artifacts and verifiable chains

Minimum SDLC evidence to include in a package:
- Commit SHAs for releases affecting production control plane
- Signed build artifacts (or checksums) with timestamped attestation
- Dependency SBOM for the release window
- SQA/regression test run ids and pass/fail summary

Incident response artifacts

When an incident is in scope for evidence collection, include:
- Incident report (P0/P1 summary), timeline, and owner
- Forensic log slice: start/end timestamps, collection method, collector_id
- Preservation manifest: list of data stores, export hashes, and storage location
- Notification history (pagerduty/smtp/slack audit) and retention assertions

Exceptions and risk acceptance workflow

This guideline treats exceptions as first-class evidence artifacts. Each exception package must contain:
1) Exception request record: id, requester, affected_control, justification, proposed compensating controls, expiration date
2) Risk acceptance memo signed by approver(s) with timestamp and reviewer comments
3) Mitigation timeline and verification checklist
4) Automated attestations verifying compensating controls are active (if applicable)

Exception lifecycle steps (numbered):
1. Submit exception via the standard exceptions portal; include scope and timeboxed request.
2. Security reviews for technical risk and legal/compliance for contract/regulatory risk.
3. Approver records decision; if approved, an exception artifact is issued with unique id.
4. Evidence collectors include exception-id in exported artifacts and route to the package index.
5. Quarterly verification: exception owners must provide artifacts proving compensating controls.

Extractors and packaging

Three extractor types (examples):
- Log-extractor (structured): queries ES/ClickHouse for tenant-range and writes JSONL with provenance header.
- RBAC-extractor: queries IAM service and outputs CSV + metadata.json describing schema version.
- SDLC-extractor: fetches build artifacts and SBOMs from CI system using signed tokens.

Packaging rules:
1) Produce a top-level manifest.json with: package_id, created_by, created_at, artifact_list (filenames), residency_assertion_hash, extractor_versions.
2) Include a redaction-manifest.txt listing fields removed and rationale.
3) Sign the package with the platform artifact signing key; store signature alongside package.
4) If package contains multi-region data, produce per-region subpackages and a master index describing mapping.

Automated commands (examples)
- Collect audit slice (CLI):
  redwood-evidence collect-logs --tenant tenant-789 --since 2027-01-01T00:00:00Z --until 2027-01-31T23:59:59Z --out /tmp/tenant789-jan2027.jsonl

- Export role catalog:
  redwood-evidence export-roles --output /tmp/roles-20270201.csv --schema-version v2

- Build package:
  redwood-evidence package --inputs /tmp/tenant789-jan2027.jsonl,/tmp/roles-20270201.csv --manifest /tmp/manifest.json --sign --out /tmp/evidence-tenant789-20270201.zip

Verification and audit checklist

For reviewers: verify all items below are present in the package and pass automated checks before acceptance:
- [ ] manifest.json with extractor versions and package_id
- [ ] residency-assertion.txt matching tenant contract
- [ ] redaction-manifest.txt explaining removed fields
- [ ] role assignment exports and role catalog snapshot
- [ ] sample audit log entries covering requested timeframe with matching request_ids to incident tickets if applicable
- [ ] SDLC artifacts or checksums for production change window
- [ ] Exception artifacts, if any, with approval signatures
- [ ] Signed package signature verification passes (platform key)

Operational ownership and SLAs

- Evidence requests from customers: handled by customer-success with security as technical reviewer; SLA 10 business days for standard requests, 72h for investigatory incidents tagged P1.
- Internal audit requests: security & compliance lead to coordinate; SLA 15 business days.
- Emergency forensic collections: eng-sre to respond within 4 hours and provide initial slice within 24 hours.

Common corner cases and guidance

- Large tenants: prefer per-service scoped exports to limit PII exposure.
- On-prem / air-gapped: provide signed attestations and extractor tooling that runs inside customer environment; do not transfer raw logs offsite unless contractually permitted.
- Legal holds: evidence packages under legal hold must be preserved beyond standard retention; add legal-hold flag to manifest.

References and related artifacts

- RBAC role certification playbook (see related pages)
- Evidence assembly matrix for regulatory audits (see related pages)
- Internal CI signing and SBOM generation standard (platform-eng)

Appendix A — Example manifest.json (minimal)

{
  "package_id": "pkg-20270201-tenant789",
  "created_by": "a.patel@redwood.ai",
  "created_at": "2027-02-01T18:02:00Z",
  "artifacts": ["audit-202701.jsonl", "roles-20270201.csv", "sdlc-checksums.txt"],
  "extractor_versions": {"log-extractor": "v1.8.0", "rbac-extractor": "v2.1.0"},
  "residency_assertion_hash": "sha256:abcd1234..."
}

Appendix B — Contact and escalation

- Primary owner: security (security@redwood.ai)
- Technical contact (evidence tooling): eng-sre (sre-evidence@redwood.ai)
- Compliance reviewer: compliance@redwood.ai
- For emergency legal escalation: legal@redwood.ai
